memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "For the breastpiece they made braided chains of pure gold, like a rope. They made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the rings to two of the corners of the breastpiece. They fastened the two gold chains to the rings at the corners of the breastpiece, and the other ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder-pieces of the ephod at the front." - Exod 39:15-18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Chains like rope, gold rings, filigree settings, fastenings at every corner. The instructions go on because the point is security.

The breastpiece was not allowed to swing loose. It had to be bound to the shoulder-pieces so that it stayed exactly where it belonged, over the priest's heart, whatever he was doing.

That word "fastened" appears repeatedly here. God did not want these names shifting or slipping.

There is real comfort in that if you have ever wondered whether you might drift out of God's care. Jesus said of His sheep that no one will snatch them out of His hand (John 10:28). Paul was convinced that nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ (Rom 8:38-39).

Notice that the chains connected the breastpiece to the shoulder-pieces. Heart and shoulders bound together. God's affection for His people and His strength to carry them are not separate systems; they are joined.

That combination is what we need. Love without power cannot save. Power without love would terrify. In Christ we have both, chained together with gold.

You are held. Not loosely.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you fear that you might drift beyond God's care?
2. Where do you need to hear that you are held securely?
3. How does joining God's love to God's strength change how you pray?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that I am fastened securely and cannot slip out of Your hand. Steady my heart in that. Amen.
